decided.singular: Cells shaded 7-9 (near black) that stand out from lighter neighbours in the 27-column calendar grid, the darkest being 316 (9), 152 and 106 (8) and day 1.
decided.recurrence: The grid wraps every 27 days. Darker cells line up loosely in columns (around +12 to +14 in several rows, and +1 in rows 136 and 163), so there is a weak 27-day recurrence. It is weak evidence, and the 27-day row width may have shaped what I saw.
decided.quarter: Rows 271-352 hold the most dark storm-like cells (273-275, 309-310, 316-317, 336) and the single darkest cell, while Q3 is visibly the lightest. Q4 is only a narrow pick over Q2 (105-106, 152-154).

answer.guess: Geomagnetic Kp index (eight 3-hourly values per day on a 0-9 scale, daily maximum shown), with 27-day solar-rotation recurrence.
